question: I have a receipt from a business meal with a client last week, but I'm not sure if I can get reimbursed. What's the limit and what do I need to include?
reference_answer: Client entertainment meals are reimbursable up to $75 per person, and you'll need to submit documentation of the business purpose along with your receipt. Make sure to submit your reimbursement request in Workday within 30 days of the expense date.

question: I work in Data & Analytics and want to work from home most of the time. What do I need to do to set up a fully remote arrangement?
reference_answer: Data & Analytics roles are flexible and can work fully remote with VP-level approval. You'll need to complete a Remote Work Agreement form from the Confluence HR template, submit it to HR via Workday by the 15th of the prior month, and go through a 6-month probationary period before the arrangement is finalized.

question: Can I share a patient's health information with a colleague in another department if they need it for their work?
reference_answer: No, you must never share patient health information (PHI) outside authorized channels. All ClaimsFlow, CareBridge, and PulseBoard data must remain confidential, and violations may result in termination and legal action.

question: What laptop options are available to me as a new hire, and when will I receive it?
reference_answer: You will receive either a MacBook Pro (M2, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) or a Dell XPS 15 (Intel i7, 16GB RAM, 512GB SSD) based on your role and team preference. Your laptop will be provisioned and ready before your first day of employment, as HR submits the equipment request at least 10 business days before your start date.

question: Can I access ClaimsFlow from my personal laptop when I'm working from home?
reference_answer: No, you must use your company laptop only, as personal devices cannot access ClaimsFlow or CareBridge. When working from home, you should use the company VPN, and your laptop will have full disk encryption enabled by IT during onboarding.

question: When do I become eligible for health insurance benefits after I'm hired?
reference_answer: Full-time employees (30+ hours weekly) become eligible for benefits on the first of the month following 30 days of employment. You'll have a separate 30-day enrollment window beginning on your first day of employment to select your plans.

question: How long does it typically take for a provider to receive payment after a claim is approved?
reference_answer: Approved claims move to Payment Batch status and are processed nightly at 11 PM ET. Payments typically reach provider bank accounts within 2-3 business days, and you can check TimeTrax under Reports > Payment History for payment confirmation logs.

question: What should I do if a claim is rejected due to an invalid member ID?
reference_answer: If a claim has rejection code 87 (Invalid Member ID), you should assign it to the Care Coordination team and tag @care-coord-leads in Slack. They will verify the member's enrollment in CareBridge to resolve the eligibility issue.

question: How often should I set my report to refresh, and what's the recommended time?
reference_answer: You can set your report to refresh on an Hourly, Daily, or Weekly basis. The document recommends setting Daily refreshes for 2 AM, and you can configure email notifications to alert stakeholders when the report updates.

question: What should I do if I left work early one day and my actual hours don't match my scheduled hours?
reference_answer: You should enter your actual hours worked in the 'Hours Worked' column, which may differ from scheduled hours if you left early, came in late, or worked overtime. For example, if you were scheduled 8 hours but left 30 minutes early for a medical appointment, you would enter 7.5 hours. It's also recommended to use the 'Notes' field to explain the reason for the deviation.

question: Who should I contact if I need help accessing the Snowflake database, and what will they help me with?
reference_answer: You should contact DBA Priya Mehta, who will schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the Snowflake instance (connection string: analytics-prod.snowflakecomputing.com). She can help you understand how to connect to and navigate the database as part of your Week 1 onboarding.

question: How long will it take to get my dataset after I submit a request?
reference_answer: The timeline depends on your selected priority level: Routine requests take 5-7 business days, Urgent requests take 2-3 business days, and Blocking requests are completed by the next business day. Data & Analytics reviews new requests every Monday and Thursday, and they'll typically respond with questions within 1 business day of submission.

question: What time should I schedule a ClaimsFlow deployment and how long should I tell stakeholders to expect the system to be down?
reference_answer: Deployments typically occur on Tuesdays and Thursdays between 2-4 PM ET to minimize impact on Claims Ops, with an expected downtime of 15 minutes. You should notify the Claims Ops Team in the #claimsflow-deploys Slack channel with the specific deployment time and expected downtime before proceeding.

question: How many claims does ClaimsFlow process each month, and what is the main benefit compared to the old system?
reference_answer: ClaimsFlow processes approximately 12,000–15,000 claims monthly across Meridian Health Partners' managed care and administrative services contracts. The system reduces manual processing time by an estimated 40% compared to the legacy system.

question: How long does it typically take for a claim to be processed from submission to payment?
reference_answer: A typical claim takes 8-12 business days from submission to either approval or denial. Approved claims are then batched and paid via ACH transfer with a 2-3 day settlement time, meaning the entire process from submission to payment is usually completed within this timeframe.

question: What time does CareBridge send its daily batch files to ClaimsFlow, and what format are they in?
reference_answer: CareBridge sends daily batch files to ClaimsFlow at 2:00 AM EST via SFTP in CSV format. These files include patient ID, service date, service code, provider NPI, units of service, and authorization reference, and follow the naming convention carebridge_claims_YYYYMMDD.csv.

question: I need to check our current denial rates and trends—which report should I look at and is there anything I should know about it?
reference_answer: You should check the Denial Analysis Dashboard, which is owned by Sarah Okonkwo and shows denial patterns by reason code and month-over-month trending. However, be aware that this report may contain stale data since it hasn't been updated since January 2024 and Sarah is currently on extended leave—contact the Claims Ops Lead (Marcus Chen) for current metrics instead.

question: What's the deadline for submitting my timesheet each week, and what happens if I miss it?
reference_answer: Timesheets must be submitted by 5 PM Friday each week. If you submit after this deadline, your timesheet will be flagged as late and may delay payroll processing by one cycle.

question: Who should I talk to if I need to understand how our claims processing system works?
reference_answer: Marcus Chen leads the ClaimsFlow Team, which owns the end-to-end claims processing system including the API layer, database schema, and batch processing jobs. The team uses Node.js and PostgreSQL, and you can find their work tracked on the `CLAIMS-PLATFORM` Jira board.

question: I just finished coding a feature and want to move my Jira ticket to Done. Should I skip the 'In Review' status?
reference_answer: No, do not skip the 'In Review' status—this is where code review happens. Tickets should move through statuses as follows: Backlog → To Do → In Progress → In Review → Done, and you should update the status daily.

question: What's the process for submitting time off at Meridian, and how much notice do I need to give?
reference_answer: You should submit PTO (Paid Time Off) requests through TimeTrax, which integrates with Workday, and you need to submit your request at least 14 days in advance. TimeTrax will automatically flag any overtime during peak seasons like March for approval.

question: How do I submit a request for a one-time analysis, and when can I expect to get it back?
reference_answer: Submit a ticket in Jira under the ANALYTICS project with the label data-request, including your business question, required metrics, deadline, and intended use. The analytics team will triage it during Monday morning standup, and simple requests that take less than 4 hours typically get committed the same day with a 2 business day SLA, while complex analysis takes 5-10 business days.

question: I have a question about my timesheet and payroll. Which Slack channel should I use to get help?
reference_answer: You should post your question in #timetrax-support, which handles TimeTrax scheduling issues, timesheet problems, and payroll questions. HR responds to questions in that channel within 4 hours during business days.

question: What should I do if I receive a critical incident alert and haven't made any progress after 10 minutes?
reference_answer: After 10 minutes without progress on P1 incidents, you should escalate to the secondary on-call engineer by checking the PagerDuty rotation for their contact information. If multiple systems are down, you should also contact the VP of Engineering (currently Sarah Chen) and page the secondary on-call.
